title: customer-phi-incident-timeline-scratchpad-alex-moreno
content:
Purpose: personal scratchpad to capture incident breadcrumbs for Customer PHI (report of degraded generation quality + intermittent 500s). Will turn into CSM update and postmortem notes.

Summary (high level):
- 2026-02-26 ~09:20 UTC: customer reports model outputs truncating and some requests returning 500s. Affects two endpoints: /v1/generate (redwood-hosted) and /v1/chat (same model).
- Impact: ~15% error rate, elevated latency (p50 ~900ms -> p50 ~1.6s), some tokens missing from responses. Customer on Dedicated pool (dedicated-us-west-2-phi).

Raw timeline + commands / hypotheses:
2026-02-26 09:23 UTC - initial report (via CSM portal)
- Customer message: "response truncated mid-sentence and got a 500 on retry"
- Action: escalated to SRE + serving-runtime.

2026-02-26 09:37 UTC - first triage (me + Priya)
- Checked Dedicated pool health: aws console shows all instances up.
- Queried metrics dashboard for dedicated-us-west-2-phi: spike in CPU on control-plane handler, modest GPU utilization, but token generation time increased.
- Quick curl test against customer endpoint (local reproduction):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" -d '{"model":"phi-2-001","input":"write a short summary of Q1 results"}' -v
  -> Response 500, body: {"error":"internal_error", "message":"unexpected end of stream"}

2026-02-26 09:50 UTC - logs pulled (serving-runtime nodes)
- Error snippet from node srv-phi-03:
  2026-02-26T09:49:51Z ERROR runtime::kv_cache - failed to fetch prefix cache: context canceled
  2026-02-26T09:49:51Z WARN  runtime::queue - request 34821 timed out after 10s waiting for batch
  2026-02-26T09:49:51Z ERROR http::handler - write response failed: write tcp 10.2.4.8:443->10.1.0.21:58732: connection reset by peer

Hypothesis A: KV cache saturation + batching backlog causing head-of-line blocking -> some requests drop with "unexpected end of stream" and connection resets.
Hypothesis B: Intermittent network blips between control-plane and serving nodes causing partial writes.
Hypothesis C: Model quantization/IO path regression (recent release 2026-02-20) introduced an edge-case for short sequences -> truncated output.

2026-02-26 10:05 UTC - experiments / commands tried
- Restarted kv-cache service on srv-phi-02 and srv-phi-03 (rolling) -> temporarily reduced 500s but spike returned in ~15m.
- Increased batch timeout from 10s -> 12s in runtime config for dedicated-us-west-2-phi (runtime-config: batch_wait_ms 12000) -> p50 latency improved slightly but 500s persisted.
- Replayed failing request patterns with --concurrency 50 from internal harness (scripts/perf/replay_phi.sh) -> reproduced 500s and saw many "timed out waiting for batch" warnings.
- Collected kernel/dmesg on srv-phi-03: nothing OOM-ish, but multiple tcp RST on port 443.

2026-02-26 10:50 UTC - routing test
- Routed 10% of traffic to cold-model-variant (phi-2-001-quantized-v1) -> no 500s observed for the routed subset but outputs were slightly lower quality (customer reported degraded phrasing).
- Suggests issue lies in primary model runtime path (maybe related to JIT/quantized kernel used by primary variant).

2026-02-26 11:25 UTC - revert attempt
- Rolled back runtime change from 2026-02-20 (reverted commit d4f5b2) on a canary node -> canary stopped returning 500s.
- Rolled rollback to 3 additional nodes -> error rate dropped to ~1-2% (baseline).

Intermediate conclusion: rolling back 2026-02-20 runtime change correlates with improved stability. Still need to confirm root cause (regression + cache/batching interactions).

Draft internal comms (short note for SRE/channel):
"Team, quick summary: Customer PHI experienced intermittent 500s and truncated outputs starting 2026-02-26 09:20 UTC. Triage indicates a regression introduced in runtime release 2026-02-20 (commit d4f5b2) which interacts poorly with KV prefix caching and batching under their workload. We rolled back the change on dedicated-us-west-2-phi and error rate reduced to baseline. Next steps: full postmortem, backport hotfix + add e2e test that simulates KV cache saturation. Action owners: Priya (root cause deep-dive + repro harness), Ethan (postmortem doc + customer-facing timeline), Alex (CSM update draft + brief on rollback steps)."

Draft CSM message to send to customer (short / friendly):
"Hi <Customer PHI contact>, thanks for reporting this. Quick update: our team identified a regression in a runtime change that, in combination with your workload's heavy prefix-caching pattern, caused intermittent 500s and truncated outputs. We rolled back the faulty change for your Dedicated pool and are seeing error rates return to normal. We expect no impact going forward while we deploy a tested fix later this week. I will keep you posted on progress and timing. — Alex (Redwood)"

Open items / TODOs:
- [ ] Priya: reproduce minimal repro and capture exact kernel/quantization path that triggers failure (target: 2026-03-01)
- [ ] Ethan: assemble postmortem skeleton and customer timeline (target: 2026-03-02)
- [ ] Alex: polish CSM note, propose customer-facing runbook for how to contact support if issues reappear (today).
- [ ] Add automated e2e test in CI that simulates: high KV cache misses + sustained concurrency 50+ for short seq lengths. (ticket JIRA-PHI-4872)

Notes / misc breadcrumbs:
- Reproduction command used: scripts/perf/replay_phi.sh --concurrency 50 --endpoint /v1/generate --token <cust-token> --input-file test-cases/phi-short-seqs.json
- Failing log pattern: "unexpected end of stream" + "failed to fetch prefix cache: context canceled" + "request .* timed out after 10s waiting for batch"
- Observed routing mitigation: routing 10% -> quantized variant removed 500s for that cohort.
- Potential long-term fix ideas: tighten batch timeouts adaptively, more aggressive prefix-cache eviction, add backpressure between KV cache and batcher.

Keep this as scratchpad until postmortem finalized. Will move to shared_drives/product/ or shared_drives/customer-success/ when ready.
